newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks tumble on consolidation, seen weak.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks tumble on consolidation, seen weak.

text.p: Thai shares closed 2.98 percent down on Tuesday amid continued profit takings by foreign investors and foreign exchange concerns, brokers said.
The composite SET index ended 18.84 points off at 614.19 on 6.2 billion baht trade. The SET-50 dipped 1.55 points to 45.72.
"Foreign investors were the major sellers as they tried to take profit (from last week's rally)," said one local broker.
"The weakening baht below 29 (baht per dollar) in the foreign exchange market today also raised more concerns about foreign exchange loss of most listed companies," he added.
Losers outnumbered gainers 231 to 100 with 55 closed unchanged.
Market sentiment is expected to remain weak tomorrow on more profit taking compounded with expected stop-loss selling, brokers said.
"Some investors are likely to make their stop-loss sellings as the market downside is expected to continue," said one broker at Thaimex Finance and Securites.
Communication shares were the top losers whose sector index dropped 8.84 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, down two baht to 163 on 444 million baht turnover.
TelecomAsia dipped 3.75 to 34.25 and Shinawatra Computer and Communication tumbled 21 to 191.
Thai Airways International rose two to 57 on expected rise in its profit boosted by the weakening baht, brokers said. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
